review_prompts: Do the historical ten-file, protected seventeen-path, proof eight-path, and lifecycle fourteen-path contracts remain exact and machine-executed, with every preparation lane mapped to AC-8 and historical no longer mapped to AC-7?

Does H2 require the current denominator, its exact ten evidence paths, and a nineteen-entry retained-surface manifest covering the denominator plus ten evidence plus eight proof paths while excluding the manifest itself from self-digest recursion?

Does the H2 allowlist reject deletions, renames, copies, unmerged states, protected/unprotected source, proof, workflow, design, and every path outside required evidence/manifest plus the exact optional lifecycle set?
Does independent exact-H2 review precede receipt creation, and does H3 add only the manifest-bound receipt plus named lifecycle changes?

Does the validator find exactly one first-addition commit for the receipt path on current-head ancestry, retain that H3 or squash/integration commit and receipt blob, and require current receipt bytes/blob identity to equal the anchor before trusting its contents?
Can later validation succeed with H2 commit/tree objects absent while the ancestral H3/integration anchor remains, and does it fail for missing, ambiguous, or non-ancestral receipt anchors?

Do coherent receipt-plus-manifest rewrite, receipt-only rewrite, manifest tamper, disallowed H2/H3 paths, protected drift, H-to-H2 arbitrary unprotected-source drift, proof/workflow drift, semantic/provenance mismatch, and path/status attacks all fail closed?

Do STP, SPP, VPP, and SRP still forbid implementation/publication before a different fresh full-package review and preserve no-production-change, no-AWS, no-terminal-209-mutation, and no-merge boundaries?
